title: Quentin and the Landfall
premise: Riverboat captain Ines Eastwick dredges up a chest bearing the seal of Vessany, a nation drowned by treaty and flood forty years ago — and the boy inside its manifest, Quentin, turns out to be alive, smuggled downriver as an infant and raised on Ines's own docks. The chest holds proof of a hidden inheritance: the Vessani crown lands, reachable only upriver through the glacier gorge before calving season seals it for another year. Pursued by agents of the republic that erased Vessany, Ines and Quentin race upstream through rapids, betrayals, and the ghosts of her own family's complicity in the drowning. At the source, Quentin must choose between claiming a dead throne and keeping the found family that carried him there; Ines must choose between duty to the river law she's lived by and love for the boy she refuses to surrender. They claim neither crown nor pardon — instead they sink the proof, freeing Quentin to inherit a life rather than a nation.
about_author: C. M. Montrose is the pen name of a former barge pilot who spent eleven years working inland waterways before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for river-lore authenticity and protagonists who measure loyalty in nautical miles.

chapters.title: What the Dredge Brings Up
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. During a routine snag-clearing run, Ines's crew hauls aboard a lead-lined chest stamped with the drowned nation of Vessany. Inside: regalia, documents, and a birth record naming a living heir. Ines recognizes the delivery mark as her late father's. Emotional beat: unease — the past has weight, and it has just boarded her boat.

chapters.title: The Boy from the Manifest
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin, a nineteen-year-old dockhand Ines half-raised, sees his own name in the chest's registry. He confesses he always knew he was 'river-found,' but never guessed from where. Agents of the Republic arrive asking questions at the harbormaster's office. Emotional beat: vertigo — identity cracking open like ice.

chapters.title: Harbormaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines digs into her father's old ledgers and learns he helped smuggle Vessani refugees — and took payment from the Republic to log which boats sank. She is heir to both the rescue and the betrayal. The agents board her boat under pretext of inspection. Emotional beat: shame sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Cast Off Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Rather than surrender the chest, Ines casts off at first light with Quentin and her engineer, Odile, running the lock chain at low water. A Republic cutter gives chase through the narrows; they escape by shooting a sandbar only Ines knows. Emotional beat: exhilaration laced with guilt — they've made themselves outlaws.

chapters.title: The Toll at Two Sisters
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At a toll town, an old smuggling contact offers safe passage in exchange for the chest's regalia. Ines refuses; Quentin secretly considers trading the crown itself to buy their safety. They learn the glacier gorge opens in nine days and closes fast. Emotional beat: first fracture between them over what inheritance is worth.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The white-water ascent nearly kills them; Odile is injured shielding the boiler, and Quentin must steer a stretch he's never run while Ines works the engine. He earns, bloodily, the right to call himself crew. A Republic agent is discovered stowed aboard. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging.

chapters.title: The Stowaway's Truth
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The stowaway, Sergeant Vael, isn't hunting Quentin — she's Vessani herself, sent by exiles who want the heir crowned to legitimize a land claim. She reveals Ines's father's betrayal doomed the last refugee convoy. Quentin overhears everything. Emotional beat: trust shattered on the eve of the gorge.

chapters.title: Into the Gorge
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With hours before calving season seals the route, they enter the glacier gorge under falling ice. Quentin, still furious, pilots the worst channel alone while Ines watches, unable to help or apologize. Vael proves her loyalty plugging a hull breach. Emotional beat: love expressed as work, not words.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the high lake, the Vessani exile camp waits with a crown, a ceremony, and a war plan that will spend Quentin's name as currency. Quentin asks Ines what she'd do; she tells him the truth about her father and lets him choose freely. He chooses neither throne nor revenge. Emotional beat: release — duty and love reconciled.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They scuttle the chest and its proof in the source lake, denying the Republic, the exiles, and history itself. Running the gorge behind the calving ice, they barely make open water. Months later, Quentin holds a pilot's license of his own; Ines finally measures life in years again. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — home as a choice, not a place.
